{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Nothing here is chosen.

WHERE IT CAME FROM: a 2026-09-28 session (Anthony with Claude, run from the dev_reflow2 project) classified every relationship declared by reflow2, StoryFlow's dynograph and market_graph against 16 candidate primitive relations, to find what a "primitive" is. Evidence: the graph-primitives design on flo2 and the primitives repo (github.com/sligara7/primitives, analysis/ — scheme, inventory pinned to reflow2 @ 4659832b, one reading per item, synthesis/ANALYSIS.md). Anthony asked, looking back on how the graphs grew, whether there was "a better way for them to build their nodes/edges to make them more efficient or correct (being correct in terms of what information the graph holds is most important)", and asked for the findings to be logged here to implement when he has time. Options offered by Claude, none chosen:

(a) A declared reading per edge type — its primitive (part-of, causes, about, norm, source-of …), sign, possibility, and which properties are modifiers — so projections are defined by meaning rather than by hand-kept lists, and a lint catches collisions with the sibling graphs (SATISFIES, SUPERSEDES, INVALIDATES, TRIGGERS and PRODUCES each mean something else in StoryFlow or market_graph).
(b) A fixed vocabulary for status values: say which values are the owner's stance (accepted), a verdict (met, passing), a lifecycle (dropped, superseded), a modality (planned, intended) or tense (an epoch before / after now).
(c) Every time anchor and ordering names its clock: design epochs (ordinal), calendar dates in properties, and the design's own change history.
(d) Who-says-so on edges: basis / asserted-by on the relations that carry a judgement, generalising what DUPLICATES.basis already does for one edge.
(e) Endpoint sorts (agent, record, rule, class, function, thing …) as the next step after the 2026-09-02 settlement that a deliberately open edge declares what it is for.

COST: (a), (b) and (c) are cheap — schema metadata plus a lint; (e) is medium (a sort per node type and a validator check); (d) is medium (an engine change on the write path).

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, kept beside the idea: the standing rule is that a distinction earns its keep only if a computation reads it — a declared reading nobody reads is decoration, so each of (a)–(e) needs a named reader before it ships; and a reading is an interpretation a later session can disagree with, so it must be revisable without a migration.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — should reflow2's schema declare what each relationship MEANS in primitive terms (a reading per edge type, a fixed vocabulary for status values, the clock of every time anchor, who-says-so on edges, the sort of thing at each end), so computations can read it?","rationale":"MEASURED 2026-09-28 (static read of reflow2 @ 4659832b; one reading per item, made by a model from schema text plus some code — a classification, not ground truth; the live server declares exactly the 65 edge types and 28 node types read). 337 items read; 213 carry a relationship, of which only 65 are edges (31%). 32 of the 56 type fields classify a node against a class that is NOT a node; 20 of 21 time anchors place a node on the clock rather than at an epoch; 10 of 13 status fields bundle several relations (Requirement.status holds the owner's stance, a verdict and a lifecycle); AUTHORED_BY carries three different relations by role (author = source, reviewer = about + stance, approver = stance on an accepted record but an assignment on a proposed one). "planned" is the commonest value across statuses, SATISFIES.coverage, DEPLOYED_TO.status and SCHEDULED_FOR.modality — every one a modality. Several relations are stored two or three ways (HAS_TEMPORAL_FACT + ABOUT_ENTITY + subject_id; VALID_FROM to an epoch + valid_from as a date; ASSESSED_ON + target_id; Verification.location restating IMPLEMENTS). One relation is misused for want of a reading: DriftEvent "references the Anchor it diverged from via DEPENDS_ON" (schema/verify.yaml:108) — a divergence drawn as a dependency. And whether change propagates along an edge already follows the SORTS at its ends: the impact table excludes the edges ending at agents (AUTHORED_BY, CLAIMS, OWNED_BY), at measurements (HAS_READINESS, HAS_OBSERVATION, ASSESSED_ON) and at the project hub (CONTAINS) — evidence that sorts are a real, currently implicit, part of what a relation is.","status":"proposed"}
